claims.text: Equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength.
Cold rolling introduces a high dislocation density into CoCrFeNiTi.
Dynamic recovery and early recrystallization rapidly reduce the cold-rolling-induced dislocation density during or after deformation.
Recovery and recrystallization limit dislocation accumulation and effective dislocation pinning.
Limited dislocation accumulation and pinning suppress the work hardening that would otherwise raise strength and hardness.
The applicable starting material is single-phase, simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi.
Conventional casting and annealing can produce a relatively defect-free grain structure in this alloy.
Systematic annealing after cold rolling can vary stored dislocation density and the extent of recovery or recrystallization.
Dislocation density and subgrain structure mediate the transition between hardening and softening regimes.
Recrystallized grains and potentially annealing twins are part of the relevant evolving microstructure.
Accelerated recovery and recrystallization explain the combination of high plasticity and machinability with low hardness and strength.
Cold-rolled samples should initially have higher dislocation density than the annealed or recrystallized starting state.
Cold rolling should produce a moderate increase in hardness.
Subsequent annealing or continued deformation under recovery-favorable conditions should reduce dislocation density through recovery or recrystallization.
Loss of dislocations should reduce strength and hardness relative to a state in which dislocations are retained.
As-cast and fully annealed recrystallized samples have low defect density and represent mechanical behavior without strain-induced dislocation structures.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar or nearly equimolar, single-phase CoCrFeNiTi under room-temperature deformation.
The proposed loading regime should be moderate enough to avoid additional phase transformations and severe localization.
